messages:
jen (AE): Quick help needed — buyer's vendor risk team asked for BCP/DR specifics for the SIG. They want RTO/RPO numbers, backup cadence, and a short description of our failover testing and evidence we can share. Need a 2-3 sentence summary + 3 bullet FAQ.

sylvie (security-eng): I can write the summary. We should include concrete numbers but avoid promising anything outside the SLA. Also attach a redacted drill summary and a sanitized runbook excerpt.

diego (solutions): Customer is a fintech POC, will be picky on RTO. Call out hosted vs dedicated differences. For hosted: typical control-plane failover <15m; for Dedicated/Private we should say "depends on customer topology, we work with you to define targets".

sam (prod): For hosted deployments: SLA is 99.9% for API availability. Operationally we aim for RTO <= 15 minutes for region/control-plane failovers; RPO is near 0 for active requests because of continuous KV/prefix replication and incremental metadata snapshots. Backups: config metadata every 5 minutes, encrypted long-term snapshots nightly with 90d default retention; customer-retention can be extended. Failover tests: quarterly tabletop + semi-annual live failover drills for core infra.

jen (AE): Perfect. Can you make that a compact paragraph I can paste into the SIG question? Also list 3 FAQ bullets to preempt follow-ups.

sylvie (security-eng): Draft paragraph: "Redwood Inference operates a multi-region, redundant serving platform. For our hosted API we target an RTO of <=15 minutes for automated control-plane and routing failovers; RPO for in-flight requests is near 0 due to continuous KV/prefix replication and incremental metadata checkpoints. Backups of critical metadata occur every 5 minutes with encrypted snapshots retained per contract. We conduct quarterly failover tabletop exercises and periodic live drills; a redacted test summary has been provided for vendor review."

diego (solutions): Suggest replacing "near 0" with "near-zero for typical request patterns (see FAQ)" to be clear.

sylvie (security-eng): Updated: "...RPO is near-zero for typical request patterns (see FAQ) ..."

artifact-bot: Uploaded sanitized-failover-summary-2025-11-08.pdf to internal-share/sales-artifacts (access: sales, security).

jen (AE): Nice. Now three short FAQ bullets please — non-technical language but concrete.

diego (solutions): FAQ bullets: 1) "How do you achieve low RTO/RPO?" — Automated routing across regions, continuous KV/prefix replication, incremental checkpoints, and health-driven traffic routing. 2) "What backups do you keep?" — Metadata/config backups every 5 minutes; encrypted snapshots nightly with default 90-day retention (custom retention available in contract). 3) "Can we witness or run a failover test?" — Yes; we offer scheduled canary failovers for POCs and will provide a sanitized test report; full audit artifacts require an NDA and redaction review.

sylvie (security-eng): If they ask for logs or full runbook, we escalate to legal/security for redaction. Also call out that Dedicated/Private deployments have different RTO/RPO tradeoffs depending on customer topology — we’ll provide architecture-specific targets during onboarding.

jen (AE): Sending to buyer now with the attached PDF. Will update here if they ask for anything deeper. Thanks all. :pray:

sam (prod): Quick note for the thread: timeline evidence in the PDF shows DNS cutover + monitoring confirmations within 11 minutes in the last drill.

jen (AE): Good to know — I'll highlight that in the cover note.

diego (solutions): Thanks team. If buyer asks for a formal SOC/ISO artifact, point them to security for existing certifications.

jen (AE): Will do. Closing thread for now — will reopen if buyer responds. :white_check_mark:
